result: Working load on the collar with a 100 kg person held: 0.99 kN; R1 static load 2.5 kN (2.5 times the working load)

200 mm trunk: load line 273 mm from the trunk axis, lever height 160 mm, friction needed 0.58 against 0.9 assumed, locking factor 1.54; at 2.5 kN the bars press 4.3 kN (2.5 kN a pad) and the chain carries 3.3 kN

300 mm trunk: load line 331 mm from the trunk axis, lever height 160 mm, friction needed 0.48 against 0.9 assumed, locking factor 1.86; at 2.5 kN the bars press 5.2 kN (3.0 kN a pad) and the chain carries 4.2 kN

450 mm trunk: load line 418 mm from the trunk axis, lever height 160 mm, friction needed 0.38 against 0.9 assumed, locking factor 2.35; at 2.5 kN the bars press 6.5 kN (3.8 kN a pad) and the chain carries 5.5 kN
Smallest locking factor 1.54 (200 mm trunk); the grip rises in step with the load, so the factor is the same at any load. Friction from the chain's full wrap round the trunk is extra and not counted
Settling at 2.5 kN: pads squash 3.1 mm at 1.9 MPa, chain seats 2.9 mm; the frame drops about 10 mm as it cocks (R1 allows 20 mm of slip)
Bearing bar (6082-T6 RHS 70 x 30 x 5): 0.48 kN m at the spine weld, 61 MPa, factor 2.0 on the heat-affected proof strength of 125 MPa at the R1 load (5.2 at the working load)

For comparison, the bar first costed for the aluminium option (RHS 50 x 25 x 3.5, the steel bar 40 % thicker) would carry 135 MPa, factor 0.92 in the heat-affected zone at the R1 load; hence the larger section
Bar to spine fillet welds (4 mm, all round): 52 MPa against 125 MPa in the heat-affected zone beside them (ER5356 weld metal 210 MPa), factor 2.4
Spine arm: 8 MPa in bending beside the lightening hole; load eye 17 mm thick with doublers, bearing 15 MPa under the carabiner bar, tear-out strength 34 kN (14 times the R1 load)

Chain cleat at 5.5 kN chain tension: 5 mm web ligament beside a slot 113 MPa (factor 1.1 in the heat-affected zone, 2.3 on the parent metal; 2.8 at the working load); twist between the two slots 0.16 kN m, 35 MPa in the cheeked top (factor 2.0). The web cannot be thickened: a link must span it. Open question O5
Chain: 5.5 kN at most at the R1 load against a working load limit of 11.2 kN and a minimum breaking force of 45 kN (factor 8.1); 2.2 kN at the working load
Rope: EN 1891 type A, at least 22 kN, about 14 kN at the figure-eight loop: factor 5.7 at the R1 load and 14 at the working load; carabiners 25 kN, factor 10 and 25
Hand force on the brake strand holding 100 kg: descender ratio 6.6, brake carabiner 1.87, hand 80 N (R5 allows 150 N); without the brake carabiner 150 N

A 25 m lowering at a steady 0.3 m/s takes 83 s and turns 24.8 kJ into heat: 85 % in the descender, 7 % in the brake carabiner, 8 % at the hand; the descender would warm by at most 44 K if it kept it all
Rope: 25 m of lowering, 1 m from the descender to the person at the start, 1.5 m for the figure-eight loop and stopper knot, 0.5 m round the brake carabiner: 28.0 m of the 30 m

Fit: 200 mm trunk: loop 769 mm (43 links), bars touch the trunk 58 mm along the pad, spine 23 mm clear of the bark; 300 mm trunk: loop 1086 mm (61 links), bars touch the trunk 87 mm along the pad, spine 31 mm clear of the bark; 450 mm trunk: loop 1563 mm (87 links), bars touch the trunk 130 mm along the pad, spine 43 mm clear of the bark; the 110-link chain leaves at least 10 links of tail on a 450 mm trunk

Rigging time once the rescuer is in position (estimate): Clip the frame to the trunk with the chain round it, link into slot, keeper and pin on 60 s; Haul the rope's loop end and the pre-rigged victim set up on the tag line 45 s; Clip the descender to the load eye and reeve the rope; brake strand over the brake carabiner 40 s; Fit the pre-rigged evacuation triangle round the hips and the chest sling 75 s; Make the one clip at height (the triangle's crotch loop) and take in all slack 30 s; total 4.2 min

Mass: collar frame 1.71 kg (aluminium weldment 1.37 kg), chain set 1.88 kg, descender 0.53 kg, carabiners 0.26 kg, rope 2.34 kg, triangle and sling 0.87 kg, bag 0.45 kg, tag line 0.30 kg, pouch 0.15 kg

Carried up the trunk by the rescuer: 4.74 kg (collar, descender, load and brake carabiners, tag line and pouch); R7 asks for under 5 kg, a margin of 257 g. The rope bag, rope and victim set (3.7 kg) stay with the helpers and are hauled up on the tag line. Whole kit 8.5 kg
The aluminium weldment (1.37 kg) saves 0.85 kg on the steel one; the bars are 0.92 kg of it, because they are sized for the heat-affected zone [C1]

Bark pressure at the R1 load: pads 1.9 MPa (0.7 MPa working), sleeved chain 0.58 MPa, bare chain links 8 MPa on a 3 mm line; the outer coconut stem is far stronger in crushing, so no cut is expected under the pads or the sleeve. Bare links outside the sleeve may mark the bark (to confirm by test)
Kit cost from the BOM: USD 802. Value-engineering target: USD 900. Estimated cost of the constructable design: USD 802 (USD 98 under the target)

R9 per-kit parts cost: USD 802, over the R9 target by USD 702; the largest lines are auto-locking rope descender with anti-panic function USD 280, evacuation triangle USD 140, lowering rope USD 105, TIG welding of the aluminium frame weldment with ER5356 filler (AC TIG) USD 45

R8: Met on paper (to confirm). Pads 1.9 MPa, sleeve 0.58 MPa at the R1 load
R9: Not met (accepted, decision 44 A). USD 802 a kit; savings sought through group purchase and one kit per climber group
